title: Parts of a Plant
keyIdea: Most plants we see have the same four main parts. Roots grow down in the soil: they hold the plant in place and take in water. The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves. Leaves catch sunlight so the plant can make its own food. Flowers make seeds that grow into new plants. A tree is a plant too: its trunk is a thick, woody stem, and its branches carry the leaves.

kid: Look at a plant. Under the soil are the roots. They hold on tight so the plant does not fall over. They drink up water too. The stem grows up out of the soil. It holds the plant up tall. Water goes up the stem like a straw.
The leaves are flat and green. They catch the sun. With sun, air and water, a plant makes its own food. It does not eat soil.
The flower is at the top. It can be bright to bring in bees. The flower makes seeds. Seeds grow into new plants.
A tree is a plant too. It has roots. Its stem is the big trunk, made of wood. Its branches hold the leaves.
adult: This is the Year 1 Plants unit of the English national curriculum, which asks pupils to 'identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees' and to 'identify and describe the basic structure of a variety of common flowering plants, including trees'. The four named parts are roots, stem (trunk), leaves and flowers. In the US, NGSS 1-LS1-1 covers how plant parts such as roots, stems, leaves, flowers and fruits help a plant survive and grow.

Each part has a job. Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and minerals. The stem supports the plant and carries water up from the roots and food made in the leaves to the rest of the plant. Leaves use light, air and water to make food (the word photosynthesis comes later, in Year 3). Flowers are where seeds are made, often helped by insects carrying pollen. A tree has the same plan: the trunk is a woody stem, and branches are side stems.

Common mistakes to watch for: thinking plants take their food from the soil (they take in water and minerals, but make food in their leaves); saying a tree is not a plant because it is big and woody; thinking flowers are only for decoration; thinking water goes in through the leaves; and calling a carrot a fruit or a stem when it is a root. Celery is a tricky one: the crunchy stalk we eat is a leaf stalk, so this lesson keeps to clearer examples.

In the lab your child builds a plant by putting each label in its place, matches each part to its job, follows blue water from the roots up to a white flower that turns blue, labels a tree, and sorts foods by the part of the plant we eat.

familyTip: Put a white flower or a pale lettuce leaf in a glass of water with a few drops of blue food colouring. Check it the next day: the colour has climbed up the stem and into the petals or leaf. Ask your child which way the water went and which part it went in through.

visual.caption: Which part does this job? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build a plant, match each part to its job, follow the water up a stem, label a tree and sort foods by the part we eat.

practice.prompt: A flower has {a} petals. One petal falls off. How many petals are left on the flower?
practice.hint: Start at {a} and count back one. The petals are part of the flower.
practice.explain: {a} take away 1 is {=a-1}, so {=a-1} petals are left. Petals help bring in bees so the flower can make seeds.

practice.prompt: A plant has {a} leaves on one side of the stem and {b} on the other. How many leaves catch the sun?
practice.hint: Count the leaves on both sides of the stem and add them together.
practice.explain: {a} and {b} make {=a+b}. All {=a+b} leaves catch sunlight to make food for the plant.

practice.prompt: Which part of a plant grows under the soil?
practice.hint: This part holds the plant in place and drinks up water.
practice.explain: Roots grow down into the soil. They hold the plant still and take in water.

practice.prompt: What is the job of a flower?
choices: To drink water from the soil
practice.hint: New plants grow from something small that the flower makes.
practice.explain: Flowers make seeds, and seeds grow into new plants. The stem holds the plant up and the roots take in water.

pool.prompt: A tree has {a} big branches. Each branch has 2 leaves. How many leaves is that?
pool.hint: Count in twos, one 2 for every branch: 2, 4, 6 and so on.
pool.explain: {a} branches with 2 leaves each makes {=a*2} leaves. The branches hold the leaves up to the sun.

pool.prompt: There are {a} plants in a pot. Each plant has one stem. How many stems are there?
pool.hint: Each plant has just one stem, so count one stem for each plant.
pool.explain: One stem for each plant, so {a} plants have {a} stems. Each stem holds its plant up.

pool.prompt: Which part catches sunlight to make food for the plant?
pool.hint: This part is often flat and green, so it can catch lots of light.
pool.explain: Leaves catch sunlight. With light, air and water, they make the plant's food.

pool.prompt: Mia says, 'A tree is not a plant. It is too big and made of wood.' Is she right?
choices: No, a tree has roots, a trunk and leaves, so it is a plant
No, a tree is an animal
pool.hint: Think about the parts a tree has. Does it have roots and leaves like other plants?
pool.explain: A tree is a plant. Its trunk is a big, woody stem, and it has roots and leaves like other plants.

pool.prompt: We eat a carrot. Which part of the plant is it?
pool.hint: Where does a carrot grow: up in the air or down in the soil?
pool.explain: A carrot grows down in the soil, so it is a root. A fruit holds seeds, and a carrot has none inside.

pool.prompt: Sam says plants eat soil to get their food. What is true?
choices: Plants make their own food in their leaves
Plants eat soil with their roots
Plants get food from their flowers
pool.hint: Roots take in water. Which part uses sunlight?
pool.explain: Plants make their own food in their leaves, using light, air and water. Roots take in water, not food.

pool.prompt: You put a white flower in blue water. Which way does the blue water go?
choices: Up the stem to the petals
Down from the petals to the stem
pool.hint: Water goes in at the bottom of the stem and climbs up like a straw.
pool.explain: The water goes up the stem to the petals, so the white petals turn blue. Stems carry water up.

pool.prompt: Which part of a tree is its stem?
pool.hint: This part goes straight up from the ground and holds the tree up.
pool.explain: The trunk is the tree's stem. It is thick and woody, holds the tree up and carries water to the branches.
